I checked each claim in the draft against the policy.

- "Good tea, no fuss." This is plain and warm, with no banned words and no superlative. "Good" is a mild descriptor, not a "best" or "finest" claim.
- "Certified organic by the Soil Association" matches the allowlist wording exactly (certificate renewed 2026).
- "packed by hand in Bristol" is a shortened form of "Every tin is packed by hand in Bristol". It says the same thing and is supported by Operations.
- "free UK delivery on orders over £25" matches the allowlist exactly.

There are no health claims, green claims beyond the allowlist, invented numbers, urgency, guarantees, or banned words. The spelling is UK-compatible. No disclosure is needed, since this is our own landing page and not a creator post or affiliate link.

Sam (marketing lead) still needs to approve it, as for everything public, but nothing in the copy needs to change.
